target_customer: US consumers paying for heart disease risk testing and prevention care (one-time $190 panel on the site), with later Medicare ACCESS program partnerships via primary care groups
problem: Heart disease is largely preventable but people do not get advanced biomarker testing or a plan. Empirical combines labs, wearable data and licensed clinicians to model risk and guide prevention.
business_model: Consumer paid lab panel and subscription care delivered through affiliated physician practices, plus partnership revenue
product_category: Preventive cardiology and AI-native primary care

founders.name: Brandon Ballinger
founders.background_notes: Education not stated on the YC page or company about page.

founders.name: Raquel Rodriguez Martinez
prior_employers: UCSF (Clinical Assistant Professor and Medical Director)
education: Trained at Kaiser and UCLA (per company about page); MD, MPP
founders.background_notes: Fitt interview says she first met Ballinger at Cardiogram as a visiting scholar.

technical_complexity.rationale: Risk modeling and wearable data integration are standard ML, but delivering licensed medical care across states adds clinical and compliance work.

defensibility.rationale: State licences and affiliated practices take effort, but lab testing and prevention programs were copyable by funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company reported growth in 2025 and a Medicare ACCESS partnership in 2026.

market_need_then: Heart disease is the leading cause of death; the company cites that 80% is preventable and consumer interest in advanced lipid markers such as ApoB was rising (company claim).

identity.voice_and_tone: Blunt and evidence-led: 'Don't die of heart disease.'

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found interviews and terms of use but no press on the brand itself; the term Empirical is shared by unrelated firms.

outcome_analysis: Empirical Health is active and says it grew 30x in 2025 and reached 30 states, with a March 2026 Beacon Health partnership under Medicare's ACCESS program. Founders pair a repeat founder with a physician. Funding amounts are not confirmed by a primary source, so the capital behind the growth is unclear.
notes: Aggregators say $500K in July 2023 (YC, Broom Ventures, Pacific 8, Pioneer Fund, Rebel Fund) and one says $3.5M with a Nov 2025 round; unverified, not recorded as amounts. Ballinger told Fitt the company raised a seed round, so a seed is recorded without amount. A search snippet shows a former legal name Slice Health, Inc. (NPPES, Sept 2022); not opened. Only Function Health was named as a competitor, via an aggregator, with no dated source, so the list is empty. Launch post names two other co-founders (Harish, Wyatt) not listed as founders on YC page, so excluded.
